text:
Sam: Heads-up — I'm seeing a ~10-12% p99 regression on small-chat workloads after the AWQ packing change we rolled yesterday. p50 looks fine, but p95/p99 jumped. Profiling points at pack/unpack and KV-copy spikes. Anyone else?
Anya: Yep, saw the same on the ded10 pool earlier today. Batch=1, seq~128. p50 stable, p95 +8ms, p99 +13ms.
Sam: Paste of quick perf summary I grabbed:```
model: red-7b-awq
config: group_size=64, pack_overlap=true
workload: api small-chat, batch=1, seq=128
before (master - 1835040000): p50=28ms p95=72ms p99=92ms
after (canary - 1835100000): p50=29ms p95=79ms p99=105ms
profile hotspots (wall time share): matmul_int8_fused: 58% | pack_ops (pack+unpack): 21% | kv_copy: 14% | other: 7%
```
Kevin: Interesting. Did the kernel selector flip to a different matmul kernel? The matmul_int8_fused share looks high but pack_ops at 21% is suspicious. Any kernel names from the trace?
Sam: Trace shows runtime picked `matmul_int8_fused_v2` on many calls but there's interleaved `pack_unpack_thread` activity. Also seeing `kv_expand_copy` on the main thread which wasn't as hot before.
Maya: I ran a microbench on my laptop (intel/rtx) quickly: toggling pack_overlap from true->false reduces main-thread CPU spikes dramatically for seq<200. For batch>4, pack_overlap helps throughput. So there's a threshold mismatch.
Anya: What were AWQ vs GPTQ weight differences? Could calibration change buffer layout and increase unpack cost?
Sam: We're on AWQ weights for the failing run (group_size=64). GPTQ tested separately earlier and didn't show same regression. So seems AWQ packing layout + pack_overlap interplay.
Kevin: Hypothesis: pack_overlap is overlapping pack/unpack with kernel execution but introduces extra KV copy contention when KV cache windows are small → increases p99 on single-request workloads. Also kernel selector may choose a pack-friendly kernel variant that has worse latency for small seq.
Maya: Agree. I also saw higher sys CPU and context switches in the canary. Quick top snippet:```
PID USER  %CPU %MEM COMMAND
3123 red   45.2  2.1  matmul_worker
3128 red   27.8  1.8  pack_unpack
3130 red   12.4  0.9  kv_handler
```
Sam: Repro steps that show the regression consistently:```bash
# reproducible client workload (local)
curl -sS -X POST http://canary-redwood/api/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"red-7b-awq","input":"hello","max_tokens":128,"stream":false}'
# run bench tool
python bench/kern_select.py --model red-7b-awq --group-size 64 --seq 128 --batch 1 --trace=brief
```
Anya: I tried a quick rollback of pack_overlap in a canary node and p99 dropped back to ~93ms. Not a full fleet test yet but promising.
perf-bot: Deploy event: canary/pack_overlap=false rolled to node i-0a12 (by Anya) — 1835123610
Kevin: If rollback helps, we should tweak heuristics instead of full revert. Proposal: change kernel chooser to prefer `matmul_int8_fused_v1` when (seq < 200 and batch <= 2 and group_size <= 64). Also add runtime flag `int8.pack_overlap_threshold` default 4 (batch) or seq threshold.
Maya: Also add lightweight tracepoints around `kv_copy` and `pack_ops` so we can measure overlap contention. I'll add a perf counter and a flame-friendly marker for pack start/end.
Sam: Action items:
- Kevin: add chooser rule + config flag, add unit test for seq/batch heuristics.
- Maya: tracepoints and sys CPU counters on KV/pack paths.
- Anya: run fleet microbench across ded pools AWQ vs GPTQ and report p50/p95/p99 delta.
- Sam: run bisect to find the exact commit that introduced the pack overlap switch for AWQ.
Anya: I'll run a 12h sweep tonight and post results in the morning, will attach raw traces (link: https://internal.gists/repro-traces/183512).
Kevin: I'll open a small PR with the chooser rule and flag. Will include perf microbench harness change: `bench/kern_select.py --chooser-debug` to dump chosen kernel per layer.
Sam: Good. If we confirm it's pack_overlap causing KV contention for small single-request hits, we should default pack_overlap=false for low-latency tiers and enable for high-throughput reserved capacity.
Maya: Also consider a lightweight pack-unpack fastpath for AWQ with group_size<=32 — lower mem copies. Might be a follow-up.
Sam: Thanks all — assigning follow-ups in the ticket. Adding :white_check_mark: when we have canary numbers back.
Anya: Noted, will update thread with numbers or rollback if needed. :thumbsup:
